title.narrative: Activity under preparation Strengthening Food Safety, Food Defence, and Fraud Measures In the South East and Eastern Europe (SEEE) Region - P114

description.narrative: Contract related to: Strengthening Food Safety, Food Defence, and Fraud Measures In the South East and Eastern Europe (SEEE) Region - P114 - Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) risks encompass a wide range of security concerns, from the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction to high-impact accidental events affecting public health. CBRN risk mitigation efforts also intersect with critical areas like infrastructure protection, climate security, counterterrorism, cybersecurity, and export controls. Most of the actions are implemented in the framework of the EU CBRN Centres of Excellence Initiative, a flagship programme launched 15 years ago, that became the ¿the EU¿s largest civilian external security programme¿ as acknowledged by the Court of Auditors. The technical nature of the cooperation in this domain, allows the EU to engage in many countries, maintain a strategic presence and continue to build trust.Objectives of this Action: 1.Improved mitigation against risks related to CBRN materials, agents and installations through the EU CBRN Centres of Excellence Initiative and associated actions Most of the actions are identified and formulated through a strategic dialogue carried out with the 63 member countries of the EU CBRN Risk Mitigation Centres of Excellence Initiative and implemented in cooperation with EU MS agencies and international organisations. This demand-driven approach ensures sustainability and ownership of the results of the interventions at national and regional levels. In parallel, global actions targeting emerging crucial risks for the EU are implemented based on a solid risk analysis and a methodology tool developed by the JRC.2.Enhanced capacities on strategic trade controls of dual-use goods The export control component contributes to advance the disarmament, non-proliferation and dual-use goods/arms control framework in non-EU countries to fully implement sanctions and strategic trade control procedures. The EU P2P Export Control Programme for Dual-use Goods is the flagship initiative of the EU to develop dialogue and cooperation with third countries, with a view to promoting the global convergence of controls, in order to support a global level-playing field and enhance international security. The priority countries are identified through a prioritisation methodology tool developed by the JRC and in consultation with DG Trade and the EEAS.This component also includes since April 2023 specific activities on sanctions such as the EU¿s sanctions outreach missions to tackle Russia/Belarus sanction circumvention in third countries whose territories and economies are used to evade efforts of Member States¿ authorities and EU operators acting in good faith, ultimately intending to weaken Russia¿s war efforts and financial resources. Priority countries are identified through an interservice steering group.3.Promote a culture of safety and responsible science and engineering With this support the EU fulfils its legal obligation vis a vis the International Science and Technology Centre (ISTC) and the Science and Technology Centre in Ukraine (STCU) ¿ two international organisations specialised in securing sensitive scientific knowledge and technical knowhow. The two centres are crucial implementing partners for several Commission¿s services (FPI, INTPA, ECHO, RTD) due to their specific areas of expertise, the presence in the region and the strong network of scientists and experts developed over the last three decades. In particular, the centres are reliable partners for the implementation of CBRN CoE and export control activities.All components will be implemented in full complementarity with bilateral and regional programmes, the Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) actions addressing the non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and ar
